must_contain: fn probe(dev: &Device<device::Core>, id_info: &Self::IdInfo) -> impl PinInit<Self, Error>;
pub fn iomap_memory(&self, start: PhysAddr, len: usize) -> Result
pub fn read_slice(&self, dst: &mut [u8], offset: usize) -> Result
pub fn write_slice(&mut self, src: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result
pub fn fill_zero(&mut self, offset: usize, len: usize) -> Result
pub fn new(ptr: UserPtr, length: usize) -> Self

pci-driver-registration-lifetime.obligation: The Rust PCI adapter must register and unregister exactly once, and the bound driver state must not outlive the kernel-managed PCI device.
pci-driver-registration-lifetime.preferred_discharge: Keep PCI registration inside `kernel::pci` RAII machinery and avoid raw driver registration calls in driver code.

pci-driver-offsetof-layout.obligation: The Rust PCI adapter must preserve the exact embedding/layout relationship between `struct pci_driver` and the generic driver core so registration glue computes the correct offset.
pci-driver-offsetof-layout.preferred_discharge: Keep the `driver::DriverLayout` impl and `DEVICE_DRIVER_OFFSET` definition inside `kernel::pci`, justified directly from the C embedding layout.

pci-device-id-layout.obligation: The Rust PCI device-id wrapper must stay layout-compatible with `struct pci_device_id`, including the location of `driver_data` used by the device table machinery.
pci-device-id-layout.preferred_discharge: Keep `DeviceId` `#[repr(transparent)]` over `bindings::pci_device_id` and centralize raw trait impls inside `kernel::pci`.

pci-device-raw-cast-lifetime.obligation: Raw conversions between C `pci_dev` storage and Rust wrappers must preserve the kernel-owned object lifetime and callback invariants.
pci-device-raw-cast-lifetime.preferred_discharge: Keep all `pci_dev` pointer casts and `drvdata` borrows in `kernel::pci`, and expose only typed references to driver code.

pci-device-send-sync.obligation: Any `Send`/`Sync` claim for the Rust PCI device wrapper must match the thread-safety guarantees of the underlying kernel device object.
pci-device-send-sync.preferred_discharge: Keep `Send`/`Sync` impls on the wrapper only, justify them from kernel device lifetime rules, and never let drivers construct raw device wrappers themselves.

miscdevice-registration-lifetime.obligation: The miscdevice registration created from PCI probe must unregister exactly once and stay valid for the lifetime of the bound driver object.
miscdevice-registration-lifetime.preferred_discharge: Store `MiscDeviceRegistration<T>` inside the driver-owned Rust state so deregistration happens via drop.

miscdevice-static-fops-sync.obligation: Any helper that marks a miscdevice `file_operations` table as `Sync` must only wrap fully initialized immutable static storage, so the driver-specific fops table can be shared without mutation races or lifetime holes.
miscdevice-static-fops-sync.preferred_discharge: Keep the `AssertSync` wrapper local to `declare_misc_device_fops!`, use it only for immutable static `file_operations` tables, and route module pinning through `fops.owner`.

miscdevice-file-private-data-lifecycle.obligation: Miscdevice file-private data must transition soundly between open, runtime callbacks, and release without double-free, use-after-free, or mismatched ownership conversions.
miscdevice-file-private-data-lifecycle.preferred_discharge: Keep file-private state ownership and borrows entirely inside `kernel::miscdevice`, with the driver only observing typed Rust state.

miscdevice-callback-ffi-bridge.obligation: The `file_operations` vtable bridge must decode raw C callback inputs into Rust wrapper types without violating aliasing, lifetime, or callback ordering invariants.
miscdevice-callback-ffi-bridge.preferred_discharge: Keep all raw callback trampolines in `kernel::miscdevice` and expose only typed trait methods to the driver.

uaccess-copy-validation.obligation: User memory reads and writes must avoid double-fetch and length/typing bugs; driver code should operate through a typed `uaccess` surface rather than raw copy helpers.
uaccess-copy-validation.preferred_discharge: Use `UserPtr`/`UserSlice`-based wrappers and validate decoded command payloads before acting on them.

uaccess-buffer-initialization.obligation: Any buffer filled from userspace must only be observed as initialized after the copy helpers report success and the initialized length is tracked correctly.
uaccess-buffer-initialization.preferred_discharge: Centralize `MaybeUninit` handling in `kernel::uaccess` and only return initialized Rust values after checked copies succeed.

uaccess-byte-reinterpretation.obligation: Byte-slice reinterpretation between typed buffers and raw userspace copy regions must preserve alignment, size, and mutability invariants.
uaccess-byte-reinterpretation.preferred_discharge: Keep byte reinterpretation helpers in `kernel::uaccess` and expose only typed read/write APIs to the driver.

uaccess-cstr-construction.obligation: Constructing C strings from userspace buffers must preserve NUL-termination and bounds guarantees before returning a `CStr` view.
uaccess-cstr-construction.preferred_discharge: Keep string-copy and `CStr` construction unsafe blocks in `kernel::uaccess`, returning only validated `CStr` values to drivers.

page-owned-ping-buffer-lifetime.obligation: The page-backed request buffer shared with the device/host must stay allocated for the lifetime of the owning Rust file state, and page-local reads/writes/copies must remain within bounds.
page-owned-ping-buffer-lifetime.preferred_discharge: Keep the buffer inside `page::Page`, expose only bounded helpers plus `phys_addr()`, and tie it to the file-owned Rust state.

vma-wrapper-lifetime.obligation: The Rust VMA wrapper must only dereference `vm_area_struct` pointers while the kernel guarantees the VMA lifetime and the documented mmap/VMA lock state.
vma-wrapper-lifetime.preferred_discharge: Keep raw `vm_area_struct` access, flag mutation, and page-insert helpers inside `kernel::mm::virt`, exposing only typed `VmaRef`/`VmaNew` methods to drivers.

vma-pfn-remap.obligation: Mapping PFNs into a userspace VMA requires proving alignment, flag, and lifetime constraints for the exported physical range.
vma-pfn-remap.preferred_discharge: Discharge this through `VmaNew::iomap_memory`, which keeps PFN-remap details inside the MM abstraction instead of the driver.

pci-io-raw-access-validity.obligation: Raw PCI BAR or config-space accesses must stay inside typed PCI I/O abstractions so address validation, resource ownership, and raw pointer conversions never leak into driver code.
pci-io-raw-access-validity.preferred_discharge: Keep raw config-space and BAR access in `kernel::pci::io`, and let drivers operate only through typed region owners and safe accessors.

shared-bar-map-lifetime.obligation: BAR/shared-memory mappings must be tied to PCI resource lifetime and unmapped exactly once on teardown.
shared-bar-map-lifetime.preferred_discharge: Discharge this through a dedicated PCI BAR owner such as `pci::SharedMemoryBar`, which owns BAR reservation and mapping teardown outside the driver.

shared-bar-map-thread-safety.obligation: Any `Send`/`Sync` claim for the shared BAR owner must match the kernel guarantees of the reserved BAR mapping and only expose thread-safe operations.
shared-bar-map-thread-safety.preferred_discharge: Keep `Send`/`Sync` on `SharedMemoryBar` inside `kernel::pci::io`, and only expose immutable metadata queries plus VMA mapping helpers to drivers.
